name: Somalia
region: Nationwide — Bay, Bakool, Lower Shabelle, Banaadir
summary: Somalia is on the brink of catastrophe. Four consecutive poor rainy seasons have produced the lowest seasonal crop harvest in 30 years, Al-Shabaab's 2025 offensive has reversed most government gains, and a 74% cut in humanitarian funding means only one in three people in need receives food aid. 6.5 million people are projected to face crisis-level hunger by early 2026.
context:
Somalia has faced near-continuous crisis for over three decades, but 2025–2026 marks a severe new deterioration. Four consecutive poor rainy seasons have devastated pastoral and farming communities that depend on seasonal rains for survival. Non-irrigated harvests in Somalia's southern breadbasket regions are projected at less than 10% of average levels — a catastrophic failure with no modern precedent.

Al-Shabaab's 2025 military offensive has reversed most of the territorial gains made by Somali government forces over the previous two years, recapturing strategic towns and expanding control across rural central and southern Somalia. The combination of active conflict, deteriorating climate, and a collapsed aid pipeline has created conditions approaching famine in multiple regions.

The humanitarian funding crisis is acute. Somalia's 2025 Humanitarian Response Plan was only 20.3% funded — receiving just $289 million of the $1.42 billion requested. This is the lowest funding rate in a decade, and the result is visible: only 1 in 3 people who need food assistance received it in October 2025. The government declared a national drought emergency in November 2025 — the first such declaration since 2022.

Over 3.5 million Somalis are internally displaced, many having fled multiple times. Malnutrition is reaching critical levels, particularly among children under five. The healthcare system, already fragile, is buckling under the combined weight of disease, injury, and funding cuts.

Somalia's crisis exemplifies the structural failures of the global humanitarian system: a country experiencing a predictable, foreseeable emergency that receives a fraction of the resources needed to prevent mass death.

donate.name: UNICEF Somalia
donate.description: Treating acutely malnourished children, providing clean water, and vaccinating against deadly disease outbreaks across Somalia.

donate.name: Save the Children — Somalia
donate.description: Providing emergency food, healthcare, and education to vulnerable children and families in Somalia's most conflict-affected areas.

donate.name: CARE Somalia
donate.description: Reaching the most isolated and food-insecure communities across Somalia with emergency nutrition and livelihoods support.

awareness: Share that Somalia's 2025 HRP was only 20.3% funded — one of the lowest rates globally — meaning most people in need received no help at all
Highlight the compounding effect of climate shocks and conflict: four failed rainy seasons plus Al-Shabaab expansion is a recipe for mass starvation
Amplify Somali voices and local journalists documenting the humanitarian crisis from inside the country
Challenge the perception that Somalia is a 'perennial' crisis that cannot be solved — targeted funding and political engagement have worked before
Raise awareness about the 1 in 3 statistic: only one-third of those who needed food in October 2025 actually received it
political: Demand that your government restore and increase funding to the Somalia Humanitarian Response Plan — at 20% funded, the response is effectively non-functional
Urge representatives to support international pressure on Al-Shabaab to allow humanitarian access in areas it controls
Advocate for climate adaptation funding for the Horn of Africa — Somalia's droughts are intensifying due to climate change
Push for debt relief and economic development support for Somalia to reduce long-term aid dependency
Support calls for sustainable agricultural investment in Somalia to build resilience against future climate shocks
